reviews.title: I miss you my Shwesandaw Pagoda
reviews.text: For many traveller Shwesandaw Pagoda of Bagan is a spiritual center point, just like reaching the top of Mt.Everest is for others. Mt.Everest has been there since times immemorial. Shwesandaw, however, is much 'younger'. According to legends circulating, Shwesandaw was built around 1057 on orders of King Anawratha as a tribute to Buddha following the conquest of the Mon and Thaton Kingdoms. Every brick seems to have been placed by famous Mon artists. This may explain its lasting fame, attracting photographers from all over the world, not to mention never ending crowds of locals who come to Shwesandaw to meditate. In 2018 people have a choice between legend and reality. Yes, reality is what the eyes can see. But nowadays what is really reality? I prefer to close my eyes and dream of the glory of Shwesandaw. Remember accessing any holy site in Myanmar requires leaving your footware and socks right next to the flight of stairs (there are four ,one on each side) you choose for a unique climbing experience. You need two strong legs, and even stronger arms. The steps are high and without the help of a bannister on one side, and strong arms, I would never reach the top. Every platform is full of people, more so as the time of sunset is drawing near. The western Mountains are right there beyond the majestic Ayerwaddy Rivers cutting Myanmar practically into East Myanmar (where Bagan's plateau of thousands of pagodas lie), and the Western side, with the coastal mountains running along

reviews.author: Gary W

reviews.title: Floating Comfort (for me)
reviews.text: Floating Comfort (for me) I never thought I would ever write about a flight, when tens of millions of people fly to all corners of the planet, but maybe somebody will be interested in a few personal remarks. As we have been flying between USA and Myanmar very frequently, our most obvious choice was China Airlines (Los Angeles to Taipei), then after about three hours and a change of plane,and about five hours later, in the morning of the following day, arrive at the beautiful and Modern Yangon International Airport. How many hours? A total of about 18. Most people arriving in Yangon will visit Bagan as part of a classic tour of Myanmar. In my case I prefer to head straight to Bagan. My personal problem was waiting 5+ hours in the Domestic terminal to catch the last flight of the day that arrives in Bagan, after stopping first at Heho to drop off people who head for the famous Inle Lake, then stopping in Bagan, and finally returning to Yangon. When you travel yearly you don't pay attention very much to legroom, seat comfort, In-flight Entertainment (except following the flight map), but Customer Service ,and Value for Money are very important for us. The flight attendants are very polite, very well trained, and speak excellent English. They hardly seem to take a rest, so many hours standing, preparing the food tray, offering refreshments, picking up blanket or head-pillows that somehow ended up on the aisle floor, passing out immigration forms, to mention some of their duties.
reviews.author: Koko D4d32

reviews.title: First experience
reviews.text: Departure from Terminal 1. Paid for slight overweight. Got official invoice for both ticket and overweight at the airport. Standard service for short domestic flight. Two times drink, warm food. Nothing special. Stewardess' were very nice. Arrival before scheduled time. I can recommend that.
